title: Deegh, Ghumer and Bharatpur (So did the (tenth) Guru got the Pathans annihilated by the Khalsa)

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the Khalsa Panth force advanced towards the South, After establishing ten contingents (Misls) of the Khalsa Panth, They laid a siege around the forces of Suraj Mai1 , Around his two forts at Deek2 and Ghumer3 . After promising to pay a ransom of seven lakh rupees, The Jat chief himself came to meet the Khalsa Panth. The way this meeting between him and S. Sham Singh took place, Dear readers, listen to the whole account of that meeting. (2)
lines: As the Khalsa Panth force advanced towards the South,
After establishing ten contingents (Misls) of the Khalsa Panth,
They laid a siege around the forces of Suraj Mai1 ,
Around his two forts at Deek2 and Ghumer3 .
After promising to pay a ransom of seven lakh rupees,
The Jat chief himself came to meet the Khalsa Panth.
The way this meeting between him and S.
Sham Singh took place,
Dear readers, listen to the whole account of that meeting.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Listen to the account about this reconciliation, As he paid a courtesy call to S. Jassa Singh Kalal. He insisted upon meeting S. Sham Singh with an embrace, Otherwise he would prefer to return without meeting. (3)
lines: Listen to the account about this reconciliation,
As he paid a courtesy call to S.
Jassa Singh Kalal.
He insisted upon meeting S.
Sham Singh with an embrace,
Otherwise he would prefer to return without meeting.

blocks.text: As S. Sham Singh refused to embrace a clean-shaven man, Both of them kept on putting up hardened postures. Thereafter, the Khalsa Panth arrived at a resolution, That S. Sham Singh should seek pardon after embracing Suraj Mai. (4)
lines: As S.
Sham Singh refused to embrace a clean-shaven man,
Both of them kept on putting up hardened postures.
Thereafter, the Khalsa Panth arrived at a resolution,
That S.
Sham Singh should seek pardon after embracing Suraj Mai.

blocks.text: As S. Sham Singh agreed to abide by Khalsa Panth's mandate, Highly delighted did Suraj Mai feel at heart. Truly would he become great after alliance with Khalsa Panth, Really had his seven lakh ransom served his purpose indeed. (5)
lines: As S.
Sham Singh agreed to abide by Khalsa Panth's mandate,
Highly delighted did Suraj Mai feel at heart.
Truly would he become great after alliance with Khalsa Panth,
Really had his seven lakh ransom served his purpose indeed.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the Khalsa Panth was holding an assembly, In a 'Sarbat Khalsa' congregation were they sitting. (Suraj Mai) arrived with a pair of horses, With excellent saddles and harness were these equipped. (6)
lines: As the Khalsa Panth was holding an assembly,
In a 'Sarbat Khalsa' congregation were they sitting.
(Suraj Mai) arrived with a pair of horses,
With excellent saddles and harness were these equipped.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As S. Shyam Singh stood up (to receive Suraj Mai), Both embraced each other exchanging greetings. Thereafter, making him seated amongst themselves, They settled the revenue that as Khalsa's subject he had to pay. (7)
lines: As S.
Shyam Singh stood up (to receive Suraj Mai),
Both embraced each other exchanging greetings.
Thereafter, making him seated amongst themselves,
They settled the revenue that as Khalsa's subject he had to pay.

blocks.text: Thereafter, reducing his revenue by one lakh as concession, He was given a hearty send off with due honours. This concession was given as a tribute to his queen, Lest the Khalsa Panth should accuse him of favouritism. (8)
lines: Thereafter, reducing his revenue by one lakh as concession,
He was given a hearty send off with due honours.
This concession was given as a tribute to his queen,
Lest the Khalsa Panth should accuse him of favouritism.

blocks.text: Promising to pay three lakh rupees immediately, The balance two lakh rupees would he pay after some time. So an amount of rupees three lakhs arrived soon, Which Suraj Mai had delivered to S. Sham Singh. (9)
lines: Promising to pay three lakh rupees immediately,
The balance two lakh rupees would he pay after some time.
So an amount of rupees three lakhs arrived soon,
Which Suraj Mai had delivered to S.
Sham Singh.

blocks.text: As the Khalsa Panth sat together to divide this amount, They started squabbling over the balance of two lakhs. Listen to the account how this squabbling came to an end, The complete details would the author narrate. (10)
lines: As the Khalsa Panth sat together to divide this amount,
They started squabbling over the balance of two lakhs.
Listen to the account how this squabbling came to an end,
The complete details would the author narrate.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As some insisted on distribution in the name of Misls, Others insisted on the strength of the individual Misls. With each sticking to their own vested interests, There arose quite a din and noise all in vain. (11)
lines: As some insisted on distribution in the name of Misls,
Others insisted on the strength of the individual Misls.
With each sticking to their own vested interests,
There arose quite a din and noise all in vain.

blocks.text: Losing two lakh rupees the way they distributed the rest, That account of distribution would he narrate. The way they disbursed it among the ten Khalsa Misls, So would he narrate about those bigger and smaller Misls. (12)
lines: Losing two lakh rupees the way they distributed the rest,
That account of distribution would he narrate.
The way they disbursed it among the ten Khalsa Misls,
So would he narrate about those bigger and smaller Misls.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

First of all, twenty five thousand were kept as a Tithe, For the service of the sacred shrine at Amritsar. The damage that was caused by Ahmed Shah Abdali, Akal Takht and Darbar Sahib needed to renovated. (13)
lines: First of all, twenty five thousand were kept as a Tithe,
For the service of the sacred shrine at Amritsar.
The damage that was caused by Ahmed Shah Abdali,
Akal Takht and Darbar Sahib needed to renovated.

blocks.text: As the surrounding periphery and steps needed repair, This amount was handed over to the caretakers. Thereafter, half of the balance amount went to Buddha Dal, Half of which amount further went to Tarun Dal. (14)
lines: As the surrounding periphery and steps needed repair,
This amount was handed over to the caretakers.
Thereafter, half of the balance amount went to Buddha Dal,
Half of which amount further went to Tarun Dal.

blocks.text: That organisation had three Misls of equal strength, Which included Shukarchakias, Ramgharias and Kanaihyias. As one and quarter share was allotted to the Bhangis, Three fourth of it went to the Nakaee's Misl. (15)
lines: That organisation had three Misls of equal strength,
Which included Shukarchakias,
Ramgharias and Kanaihyias.
As one and quarter share was allotted to the Bhangis,
Three fourth of it went to the Nakaee's Misl.

blocks.text: Similarly, S. Sham Singh's Misl had a larger strength, As it consisted of twelve thousand soldiers. Three fourth share of the ransom amount received, Was it allotted to the share of Sangat Singhia Misl. (16)
lines: Similarly,
S.
Sham Singh's Misl had a larger strength,
As it consisted of twelve thousand soldiers.
Three fourth share of the ransom amount received,
Was it allotted to the share of Sangat Singhia Misl.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The third Misl belonged to the Dallewalias, Much strength had it gained in the Doaba region. As they had no considerable share in the Majha region, They had their headquarters at village Dhabanwala. (17)
lines: The third Misl belonged to the Dallewalias,
Much strength had it gained in the Doaba region.
As they had no considerable share in the Majha region,
They had their headquarters at village Dhabanwala.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
The fourth Misl consisted of Singhpurias, The Ahluwalias were also formed a part of it. The fifth consisted of some selected Singhs, Who were known as belonging to Amritsaria Misl. (18)
lines: The fourth Misl consisted of Singhpurias,
The Ahluwalias were also formed a part of it.
The fifth consisted of some selected Singhs,
Who were known as belonging to Amritsaria Misl.

blocks.text: Another Misl consisted of older, younger brave Singhs, Who hailed from the Sodhis, Bedis, Trehans and Bhallas. Thus, the whole amount was distributed among ten Misls, These ten Khalsa Misls resembled the Yadava4 's organization. (19)
lines: Another Misl consisted of older, younger brave Singhs,
Who hailed from the Sodhis,
Bedis,
Trehans and Bhallas.
Thus, the whole amount was distributed among ten Misls,
These ten Khalsa Misls resembled the Yadava4 's organization.

blocks.text: Dohra:
As there were ten Misls of the Yadav clan, So there were ten Misls in the Khalsa Panth. As Lord Krishna commanded the ten Yadav Misls, The tenth Sikh Guru directed the Khalsa Misls. (20)
lines: As there were ten Misls of the Yadav clan,
So there were ten Misls in the Khalsa Panth.
As Lord Krishna commanded the ten Yadav Misls,
The tenth Sikh Guru directed the Khalsa Misls.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
As the Yadavs escaped Kaljaman's5 onslaught, So would the Singhs escape Abdali's invasion. The number of times Jamankal invaded the Yadavs, The same number of times Abdali invaded the Singhs. (21)
lines: As the Yadavs escaped Kaljaman's5 onslaught,
So would the Singhs escape Abdali's invasion.
The number of times Jamankal invaded the Yadavs,
The same number of times Abdali invaded the Singhs.

blocks.text: As Lord Krishna got Kaljaman destroyed by the Yadavs, So did the tenth Guru got Abdali decimated by the Khalsa. As all the Muslim rulers were annihilated by the Khalsa, The Khalsa Panth shouted slogans of Guru's victory. (22)
lines: As Lord Krishna got Kaljaman destroyed by the Yadavs,
So did the tenth Guru got Abdali decimated by the Khalsa.
As all the Muslim rulers were annihilated by the Khalsa,
The Khalsa Panth shouted slogans of Guru's victory.
